subject: Logic 13 track-header Volume fader: an AXIncrement, AXDecrement or AXValue write is readable at once, so the time of mixer.set_volume was fixed sleeps in front of readbacks
question: On Logic 13 how long after an Accessibility write on a track-header Volume fader does its AXValue read the new value?

reverify.command: On a disposable copy of a five-track project in Logic 13, start one LogicProMCP server and call logic_mixer set_volume 20 times on the same track with values 0.72 and 0.45 alternating, timing each call from the client, then read the track's header fader with a separate Accessibility reader.
reverify.expected: Every call returns State A with verified true and reached_exact true; the median call is under 150 ms; the reader shows the last requested value.
reverify.cost: A disposable project copy; about 2 minutes; no save.

method: Built main at 9664b4f1 and called logic_mixer set_volume 20 times on track index 2 of a copy of the R11 fixture in one server process, timing each call; repeated the run with temporary timers in the write path to split locate, nudge and fine phases. Built the settle-poll repair (no element cache; every call locates the fader in the current window) and called set_volume 10 times alternating 0.72 and 0.45 in one process, timing each call. Every call's envelope was recorded.

observations.what: before, split of one call, ms
fixed sleep before each readback in the unrepaired write loop, ms
observations.reads_after_the_repair: the first read after each write already returned the new value in the 13 steps of a call

observations.what: after, settle poll with confirming read and a settled final sample, no cache, 10 calls, wall ms
observations.note: each call locates the fader in the current window again (70 to 95 ms) plus the confirmed reads

conclusion: On this host the header Volume fader reads its new AXValue immediately after each write; the fixed 25 ms sleep before every readback was most of a call. Polling from the first read, accepting a changed value only when a second read one step later agrees, took the median from 530 ms to about 105 ms with the same State A; the remaining time is the full current-window locate on every call.
limits: One Logic 13.0 build 7801 host, ko-KR, one fixture, one track, header Volume fader only.
The per-part split of a before-call comes from temporary timers and is not committed.
A transient value passing through the target is covered by a unit test with a scripted slider, not measured live.
The evidence files are retained under the author's cache and are not committed.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record measures call latency and write readback timing. It adds no Apple label vocabulary and claims no string-corpus value.
